result.title: Gaussifier: Fast 2D Gaussian Decomposition
result.summary: 2D Gaussians render images at thousands of frames per second. However, fitting an image takes seconds of optimization. This confines 2D Gaussians to offline use. Feedforward methods are faster but less accurate without per-image fine-tuning. We present Gaussifier, a lightweight feedforward framework for 2D Gaussian decomposition. We learn a density map of Gaussian centers from per-image fitting data. Equal-mass Voronoi places Gaussians so that each Voronoi cell holds approximately equal density. A stateless, reusable network then refines the output in a few iterations. Gaussifier reaches 40.73/38.61\,dB PSNR on Kodak-24/DIV2K at over 60 FPS. At the same Gaussian count, it exceeds every feedforward baseline by 3.0 to 15.6\,dB in PSNR. With fewer Gaussians than any baseline, it still leads the strongest one by 2.5 to 3.5\,dB. At the same count, baselines with their own per-image fitting need 26 to 326 times longer to reach its PSNR. Gaussifier makes high-fidelity 2D Gaussian images fast and light enough for real-time applications. We release code, weights and a browser-based WebGPU demo at https://github.com/Gaussifier/gaussifier.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Gaussifier，一个轻量前馈框架，用于把图像分解为 2D Gaussians：先从逐图拟合数据学习 Gaussian 中心的密度图，用等质量 Voronoi 划分分配高斯位置，再由可复用的无状态网络迭代精修，从而在 60 FPS 以上达到较高 PSNR。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按密度自适应分配表示单元、以及无状态网络迭代精修输出的思路，可能为视觉 token/状态容量分配与迭代式 latent 精修提供可核查线索，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理，联系较远。
